reply:
I can't run any bash commands beyond the earlier `npm test` in this session — further shell invocations require approval and there's no approval surface available. The automated test run (which did succeed) is my verification.

**What changed:** `habit done <name> [when]` now accepts an optional trailing date argument — `today`, `yesterday`, or an ISO date like `2026-09-01`. Parsing lives in `commands.js`/`streak.js` (new `parseDateArg` in `streak.js`), so `cli.js` needed no changes. Added 3 tests covering explicit ISO dates, `yesterday`, and multi-word habit names that don't end in a date; all 10 tests pass.

One decision worth flagging: a two-word habit name whose last word happens to look like a date (e.g. `habit done "trip 2026-09-01"` as a literal name) will be parsed as name `trip` + date `2026-09-01` rather than a literal name — this seemed like the right tradeoff since real dated entries are far more common than habit names ending in a date-shaped word, but let me know if you'd rather require a flag (e.g. `--on`) to disambiguate.
